history: Anciently called Chang'an, it served as capital for 13 dynasties — Western Zhou, Qin, Western Han, Sui, Tang and more — over 1,000 years of capital history. It ranks with Athens, Rome and Cairo as one of the world's four great ancient capitals. The Silk Road set out from here, camel bells ringing all the way to Rome. The Terracotta Army is the Eighth Wonder of the World; the Ming City Wall is the best-preserved ancient wall. Today it is a national central city and a powerhouse of science, education, aerospace and defense.
importance: Capital of 13 dynasties · First batch National Historical City
foods: Baiji flatbread stuffed with braised pork — called the ancestor of the Chinese hamburger.
You tear the bread yourself into the rich mutton broth — a ritual as tasty as the soup.
Belt-wide noodles with oil-splashed chili, named after a legendary 58-stroke character.
Sour, spicy and refreshing — a summer special. The gluten bits are the soul.
Pork-intestine paomo, named after the gourd of the medicine king Sun Simiao.
Sticky-sweet jujube and sticky-rice cake — the morning aroma of the Muslim Quarter.
Beef-ball and veggie stew with bread chunks — Xi'an's hardcore breakfast.
Huanggui persimmon cakes made from Lintong fire-crystal persimmons, crispy outside, soft inside.
A ladle of hot oil 'sizzles' over chili on the noodles — the aroma is instant.
A Tang palace cold dish: cold zongzi with honey and osmanthus sauce, perfect for summer.
scenes: The Eighth Wonder of the World — a two-thousand-year-old underground army.
The best-preserved ancient city wall: a 13.7 km loop you can cycle on top.
The sutra pagoda built under monk Xuanzang — a Tang-dynasty Buddhist landmark.
A thousand-year-old Muslim quarter; snack aromas drift over the flagstone streets.
The royal hot springs where Lady Yang bathed, at the foot of Mount Li.
The Ming city center — 'evening drums and morning bells', the memory of the old city.
Ruins of the great Tang palace, four times the size of the Forbidden City.
The Tang-era Jianfu Temple pagoda — 'Morning Bell at the Wild Goose Pagoda', one of the Eight Sights.
A treasure house of Chinese civilization: 'Give me a day, I'll give you 10,000 years.'
The Tang-style night street made famous by the tumbler-performing girls.
